title: Front Suspension: What Supports, Guides and Pivots
introduction: The front suspension has to carry the car, let the wheels move over bumps and still let them steer. I separate those jobs before the parts become a vocabulary traffic jam: the spring supports load, the strut controls motion and helps locate the wheel, and the lower arms guide the lower steering pivots. This overview explains the component lineup and its relationships; it does not teach inspection, disassembly or alignment.

edits.why: The list identifies the parts in this front suspension, including both front and rear lower arms within that assembly.

edits.text: Front and rear lower arms — locating links that guide the lower end of the steering spindle or knuckle while allowing suspension movement.
edits.why: “Front and rear” distinguishes the lower arms in this front-suspension layout; it does not move the rear-named arm into the rear suspension.

edits.text: Stabilizer bar and links — the linked bar arrangement that helps resist side-to-side body roll.
edits.why: Roll resistance is a different job from supporting the vehicle’s load or damping suspension movement.

edits.text: Strut and spring assembly — combines a surrounding coil spring with the strut’s damping and structural locating functions.
edits.why: The spring stores and releases energy as it moves; the strut’s shock-absorber function controls that motion. Sharing an assembly does not make their jobs identical.

edits.text: Wheel bearing and wheel hub — the bearing allows the hub to rotate while carrying load, and the hub supports the mounted wheel.
edits.why: This pairing explains wheel rotation and support without establishing whether the parts are serviced separately or together.

edits.text: Wheel spindle — the steering member whose pivot relationships are described below.
edits.why: Read the spindle together with the strut and lower-arm connections to understand how the wheel can steer while the suspension moves.

edits.text: In this front suspension, the strut assembly takes the place of an upper arm and ball joint. A coil spring surrounds the strut, which also performs the shock-absorber function. Together, the strut and spring assembly supports vehicle weight and provides a pivot point for the steering spindle. Front and rear lower control arms and ball joints provide the lower (unloaded) pivot points for the steering spindle and/or knuckle.
edits.why: I read the layout from the upper locating relationship down to the lower pivots. The strut is more than a damper bolted nearby: it also belongs to the structure that locates the steering member. The spring carries load while damping controls how the resulting movement settles.
